title: TiDEomics Tutorial
text: TiDEomics (Time-course Differential Expression analysis omics data) R package multi-group time-course omics analysis built SummarizedExperiment, especially comparison two conditions across time. TiDEomics provides: integrated workflow data processing functional interpretation, different omics data types feature x sample matrix format, handling missing values. approach separate time-dominant, group-dominant, group-specific temporal effects combination pairwise differential expression, variance decomposition, co-expression module analysis (WGCNA). filtering strategy based residual variance mixed-model variance decomposition, prioritising features structured differential expression unexplained variation. comparison, traditional filtering total variance coefficient variation less appropriate biological variation across groups time course expected. Existing packages time-course omics analysis available, typically designed transcriptomics data. packages limited two-group comparisons (e.g. splineTimeR) expect raw sequencing counts (e.g. ImpulseDE2, TCseq). maSigPro supports multi-group time-course DE analysis via polynomial regression, complementary TiDEomics fewer assumptions temporal trends. TiDEomics also integrates QC, filtering downstream functional enrichment within workflow. TiDEomics incorporates Trendy (Bacher et al. 2018) operates single time series estimate breakpoints per group per feature, derived variance decomposition PALMO (Vasaikar et al. 2023) introduced residual variance filtering criterion. tutorial demonstrates basic workflow, explains key parameters, gives practical tips. Key features covered: Preparing input: Create SummarizedExperiment object data matrix sample annotation, checks correct formatting. Quality control: Visualise value distributions missingness patterns. Normalisation, grouping merging replicates: Normalise feature starting time point focused changes baseline. Transform data analyses require single groups single time series. Sample relationships visualisation (correlation matrix, PCA, UMAP): Explore global structure major sources variance, check batch effects, identify features driving PCs. Pairwise differential expression (time group): Identify DE features pairs time points within group, pairs groups time point. Classification feature property (randomness overall fold change): Classify features different categories (e.g., non-random vs. random, differentially expressed vs. stable) based properties including trend significance maximum fold change. Segmented regression Trendy: Estimate breakpoints feature group summarise dynamic patterns. Variance decomposition modified PALMO: Quantify relative contributions Time, Group, Residual, distinguish time group-dependent DE features “noisy” features. Module identification WGCNA: Identify co-expression modules different temporal group-specific patterns. Functional enrichment (gene ontology, drugs, etc.): Interpret biological meaning identified DE features modules.

title: TiDEomics Tutorial
text: TiDEomics expects: rows: features (e.g. genes, proteins) columns: First column feature identifiers. columns numeric measurements features sample. Missing values (NA) allowed. Sample: sample names, match column names data Group: experimental group Time: numeric time point Replicate: replicate ID (optional, auto-generated absent) Batch: batch ID (optional) Subject: biological subject ID repeated-measures designs (optional, set via subject_col) Example: subset GSE263759 data set published Traxler et al. (2025). Ensembl IDs mapped symbols, genes zero counts excluded. Use time 0 untreated samples groups’ time 0. Sample 500 random genes. Normalised log2(CPM + 1)

text: normalise_to_start() subtracts baseline value feature starting time point (referred time 0) first available time point feature missing time 0. Two modes available defining baseline: by_subject = FALSE (default): group-level baseline, mean samples starting time point group. used subject-level information available -subject baseline differences interest. by_subject = TRUE: subject-level baseline, mean samples starting time point subject. used subject-level information available focus subject-specific changes baseline. original time-0 normalised data stored SummarizedExperiment object downstream functions allow user specify use analysis (assay = 1 'orig' original, assay = 2 'norm' time-0 normalised). Use original data absolute abundance differences across groups interest (e.g., constitutively different baseline levels). Use time-0 normalised data relative changes baseline interest.

title: TiDEomics Tutorial
text: two DE functions pairwise comparison time points groups built based limma package (Ritchie et al. 2015). DE_between_time(): Compare pairs time points within group. Output: Nested lists DE statistics tables, including features significant features. Use plot_DE_between_time() summarise number DE features per pair time points per group. Subject column provided via subject_col create_input(), DE_between_time() automatically uses paired design via limma::duplicateCorrelation(block = Subject). DE_between_group(): Compare pairs groups time point. Output: Nested lists DE statistics tables, including features significant features. Use plot_DE_between_group() summarise number DE features per pair groups line plots. Common parameters functions: assay: index assay use (1 = original, 2 = time0-normalised available) filter: minimal number non-NA replicates feature included DE testing (e.g., filter = 1 means requiring features least 1 non-NA value time points specific group, groups specific time point). trend: passed limma::eBayes(). Set TRUE RNA-seq count-derived data model mean-variance trend. FALSE (default) usually appropriate types data, trend typically weak. trend can visualised limma::plotSA() elements $fit_list functions’ output. Default thresholds DE p.adj < 0.05 |log2FC| > 1. plot_DE_between_time() plot_DE_between_group() allow re-filtering DE setting new thresholds. Please note example data two replicates per time point. replicates recommended robust pairwise DE analysis. title: TiDEomics Tutorial
text: calc_feature_property() computes per-feature properties: P_trend: calculated randtests::bartels.rank.test(), testing non-randomness time profile (.e., whether feature shows significant overall trend across time points). Max_FC: maximum fold change across time points, calculated difference feature’s maximum minimum abundance across time points. captures overall magnitude change across time course, regardless specific time points changes occur. Max_FC_time: difference time points maximum minimum abundance, providing information direction () duration changing. Exp_threshold: user-set value threshold feature considered expressed sample. can used filter features based expression level, e.g. setting threshold = 0 means values > 0 (log2(CPM + 1) > 0, .e. CPM > 0 tutorial dataset) considered expressed. default NULL, means non-NA values considered expressed. T_total, T_exp Exp_ratio: number total time points, number expressed time points values > Exp_threshold (non-NA values threshold = NULL), proportion expressed time points (T_exp / T_total). Rho_time: Spearman correlation time (positive = , negative = ). Requires least 3 expressed time points. Peak_ratio: proportion time points local maxima (0 = monotonic, higher = oscillatory). Log2_CV: log2(1 + SD / |mean|), coefficient variation relative temporal variability. AUC: area time-0-normalised curve assay 2. Positive = net increase baseline, negative = net decrease. NA assay 2 available (run normalise_to_start() first). property values can used classify features different categories (e.g., non-random vs. random, differentially expressed vs. stable) downstream analysis interpretation. example, features P_trend < 0.05 Max_FC >= 1 can candidates non-randomly overall-changing DE features. Note: replicates present, input mean replicates time point, output merge_replicates(). function set require least 3 values > threshold calculate P_trend. Features expressed one group subset groups can extracted group_specific_features() based output table summarise_feature_property().

title: TiDEomics Tutorial
text: Variance feature decomposed linear mixed models (LMM) contributions Group, Subject (present), Time, Residual, optionally Group:Time (Subject:Time) interaction, captures group-specific temporal patterns. helps identify time-dependent features, group-dependent features, “noisy” features high residual variance. Interpreting components: High Time: time-dependent features, dynamic along time course consistently across groups. Good candidates run_Trendy() time-focused analysis. High Group: group-dependent features, stable along time differentially expressed groups. May baseline biological markers. High Subject (present): features baseline differences individuals, biologically meaningful patient studies. High Residual: unexplained variation, consider excluding downstream analysis. function decomp_variance() inspired PALMO::lmeVariance()(Vasaikar et al. 2023). Group Time always included (auto-skipped 1 group time point present). Subject included present colData. Set interaction = TRUE add Group:Time (Subject:Time Subject) variance component capturing group-specific temporal patterns. Sufficient replicates per combination required stable estimates.
code: # filter genes for variance decomposition: # at least 50% values > 0 in at least 2 groups decomp_filter_genes <- group_specific_features(property_tb,     filter_ratio = 0.5,     group_pct = 2 / 4,     GO = FALSE, genename = FALSE )$features #> Filtering criteria: >=50% values >0 in >=2 of groups: IFNbeta, IFNgamma, LPS, untreated  var_decomp <- decomp_variance(data_obj,     features = decomp_filter_genes,     assay = 1, core = 2 ) #> LMM: exp ~ (1|Group) + (1|Time)  |  Output: Group, Time, Residual  plot_variance(var_decomp, rank = "Time", top_n = 20) #> Features not specified. Plotting top 20 features ranked by Time. plot_variance(var_decomp, rank = "Group", top_n = 20) #> Features not specified. Plotting top 20 features ranked by Group.

text: TiDEomics wrap clusterProfiler::enrichGO() clusterProfiler::gseGO()(Yu 2024; Xu et al. 2024; Wu et al. 2021; Yu et al. 2012) run GO enrichment efficiently gene sets ranked gene list. ranked gene list (e.g., ranked Time Group contribution variance decomposition), use enrichGO_rank() plot enrichplot::gseaplot2().  multiple defined gene sets (e.g. WGCNA modules, DE genes feature classification), use enrichGO_list() plot plot_GO(). Optionally, use simplify = TRUE enrichGO_list() simplify GO results removing redundant terms (default: FALSE).    Enrichment can also performed Molecular Signatures Database (MSigDB) via enrich_msigdb(), queries gene sets msigdbr::msigdbr() runs hypergeometric test across user-selected collections (Hallmark, GO, etc.) specific gene sets. title: TiDEomics Tutorial
text: Enriched terms can added module profile plot plot_modules_h(), similar plot_modules_v() horizontally aligned annotation modules top enriched GO terms. plotting function adapted ClusterGVis package (Zhang et al. 2026).  Multiple enrichment categories (e.g. GO BP, CC, MF, MSigDB collections, enrichR databases) can displayed side--side passing vector enrich_category. Features interest can marked heatmap shown annotation column via mark_features enrich_category = "Hub features". enrich_p_threshold parameter controls per-category p-value colour-coding enrichment terms; set NA “Hub features”, use auto-assigned colours instead. title: TiDEomics Tutorial
text: prepare_tide() wrapper function runs multiple preprocessing steps single call, including input creation, normalisation, merging replicates, variance decomposition, feature filtering. convenient standard analyses, running step individually allows control parameters. Variance decomposition filtering run "orig" "norm" assays. returned list tide contains: Pairwise DE, WGCNA enrichment can run returned elements, results can appended list centralised storage.
code: tide <- prepare_tide(     data = tutorial_data,     sample_ann = tutorial_sample_info,     filter_ratio = 0.5,     min_groups = 2,     keep = "below_quantile",     residual_threshold = 0.75 ) #> No Subject column specified. Samples treated as independent. For repeated-measures designs, set subject_col to the column identifying biological subjects. #> Converting 'Group' column to factor. Default order is alphabetical. #> Converting 'Replicate' column to factor. Default order is numerical. #> Converting 'Batch' column to factor. Default order is numerical. #> Normalising to group baseline at each feature's first non-NA time point. #> Preparing TiDEomics input: 500 features, 40 samples, 4 groups #> Filtering criteria: >=50% values >0 in >=2 of groups: IFNbeta, IFNgamma, LPS, untreated #> Cross-group filter (Exp_ratio >= 0.5 in >= 2 groups): kept 340 of 500 features (68%) #> --- assay: orig --- #> LMM: exp ~ (1|Group) + (1|Time)  |  Output: Group, Time, Residual #> Residual filter (below_quantile): kept 255 of 340 features (75%) #> --- assay: norm --- #> LMM: exp ~ (1|Group) + (1|Time)  |  Output: Group, Time, Residual #> Residual filter (below_quantile): kept 255 of 340 features (75%) tide$filter_summary #>                stage assay n_features pct_kept                       threshold #> 1              input  <NA>        500      100                            <NA> #> 2 cross_group_filter  <NA>        340       68 Exp_ratio >= 0.5 in >= 2 groups #> 3    residual_filter  orig        255       51          below_quantile = 69.03 #> 4    residual_filter  norm        255       51          below_quantile = 69.03 tide$DE <- list(     between_group = DE_between_group_out,     between_time  = DE_between_time_out ) tide$WGCNA <- net  tide$enrichment$GO_modules <- go_list tide$enrichment$MSigDB <- hallmark_msigdb tide$enrichment$GO_group <- gse_group

title: TiDEomics Tutorial
text: TiDEomics supports two experimental designs, auto-detected sample annotation: Cell culture / independent samples: create_input(data, sample_ann) – sample independent. LMM uses (1|Group) + (1|Time). DE uses unpaired designs. Patient / repeated-measures: create_input(data, sample_ann, subject_col = "PatientID") – subjects tracked across time points. LMM adds (1|Subject). DE_between_time() uses paired design via limma::duplicateCorrelation(). normalise_to_start(by_subject = TRUE) subtracts subject’s baseline. merge_replicates() plot_trend() compute statistics across subjects. Users can ask different biological questions use different functions TiDEomics answer . example: features change time sample group? -> DE_between_time(), calc_feature_property(), run_Trendy(). features differ groups time point? -> DE_between_group() (starting time point, use assay = 1; later time points, use assay = 1 original input data, use assay = 2 change--baseline). temporal pattern individual features? -> run_Trendy() + summarise_Trendy() + extract_segment_trends(). features noisy vs biologically driven? -> decomp_variance() + plot_variance(), noisiness can represented Residual variance. co-expression modules present temporal profiles? -> prepare_WGCNA() + run_WGCNA() + plot_modules_v() plot_modules_h(). biological processes associated genes interest (e.g. co-expression modules, differentially expressed genes sample group)? -> enrichGO_list() + plot_GO(). biological processes associated genes ranked property (e.g. time group contributed variance)? -> enrichGO_rank(). normalise data? -> normalise_to_start() focus changes baseline; apply global normalisation (quantile, median) batch correction appropriate, create_input(). handle missing values? -> impute_groups() run_Trendy. plot_pca() plot_umap() automatically exclude features missing values. prepare_WGCNA() filter features many missing values.

what: Time-course Differential Expression analysis of omics data
title: Time-course Differential Expression analysis of omics data
text: TiDEomics provides integrated framework Time-course Differential Expression analysis omics data multiple experimental groups / conditions. TiDEomics enables: Analysis feature x sample format data different omics technologies. Comparison multiple (two) time courses systematically. Filtering features residual variance, accounting group temporal structure. Identification features (e.g. genes, proteins) pathways differentially expressed time, group, factors (time x group interactions). Integration quality control, data processing, sample-level feature-level analysis, tailored time-course multi-condition data. Functional enrichment high-quality visualisation. Existing time-course analysis tools typically focus single analysis step limited two-group designs transcriptomics input, provide integrated workflow.  Example applications include: Transcriptomics analysis cell type’s response different stimuli time. Proteomics analysis wild type multiple mutant cell lines sampled several time points. TiDEomics supports datasets missing values (e.g. mass spectrometry-based proteomics), operates SummarizedExperiment objects ensure compatibility Bioconductor ecosystem. TiDEomics supports independent-sample designs (e.g. cell culture) repeated-measures designs (e.g. patient longitudinal studies, via subject_col create_input()). Downstream functions auto-detect data structure.

title: Calculate feature property — calc_feature_property
text: list SummarizedExperiment objects, corresponding one group, updated rowData containing following columns: Feature, Group, Exp_threshold, T_exp (number time points values > Exp_threshold), T_total (total number time points), P_trend (p-value Bartels' test randomness trend), Max_FC (maximum fold change across time points), Max_FC_time (difference time points maximum minimum expression occur; positive max occurs min, negative otherwise), Exp_ratio (T_exp / T_total), Rho_time (Spearman correlation time; positive = trend), Peak_ratio (number local maxima / T_total; 0 = peaks detected), Log2_CV (log2(1 + CV) expression across time points), AUC (area time-0-normalised curve assay 2; NA assay 2 available).

'Replicate' 'Batch' optional columns auto-generated provided. 'Time', 'Replicate' 'Batch' numeric. subject_col Optional: name column sample_ann identifying biological subjects measured repeatedly across time points (e.g., "PatientID"). provided, column renamed 'Subject' used repeated-measures analyses downstream. NULL (default), samples treated independent, e.g. cell culture experiments. replicate_col Optional: name column sample_ann identifying replicate IDs. provided, column renamed 'Replicate'. NULL (default), function looks column named 'Replicate'; absent, replicate IDs auto-generated within Group Time (Subject, provided). batch_col Optional: name column sample_ann identifying batch information. provided, column renamed 'Batch'. NULL (default), function looks column named 'Batch'; absent, samples assigned batch 1.

title: Gene set enrichment via MSigDB — enrich_msigdb
text: gene_list named list gene vectors, data.frame Feature Module columns WGCNA_module(). universe Background genes (required). category MSigDB category (default: NULL). See msigdbr::msigdbr_collections(db_species = "HS"/"MM") available options. required gene_sets provided; case collections searched locate named gene sets. subcategory MSigDB subcategory (default: NULL). Set NULL include subcategories category. gene_sets Optional character vector specific MSigDB gene set names include (e.g., c("HALLMARK_APOPTOSIS", "HALLMARK_P53_PATHWAY")). provided, msigdbr queried across collections find gene sets, category subcategory required. NULL (default), gene sets category/subcategory used. species Species input genes (default: "Homo sapiens"). See msigdbr::msigdbr_species() available options. db_species Species MSigDB genesets (default: "HS"). Use "MM" mouse-native gene sets. species db_species mismatch, db_species MSigDB used ortholog mapping species. name Name output list element. NULL, auto-derived category (e.g., "C2" names output element "C2"). category also NULL, uses "msigdb". pvalueCutoff Adjusted p-value cutoff (default: 0.05). pAdjustMethod P-value adjustment method (default: "BH"). minGSSize Minimum gene set size (default: 10). maxGSSize Maximum gene set size (default: 500).

title: Prepare TiDEomics input — prepare_tide
text: data data frame rows features (e.g., genes, proteins) columns samples. first column contain feature identifiers (e.g., gene symbols) named 'Feature'. data normalised log transformed. Missing values allowed. sample_ann data frame containing sample annotations required columns: 'Sample', 'Group', 'Time'. 'Replicate' 'Batch' optional columns auto-generated provided. 'Time', 'Replicate' 'Batch' numeric. subject_col Optional: name column sample_ann identifying biological subjects measured repeatedly across time points (e.g., "PatientID"). provided, column renamed 'Subject' used repeated-measures analyses downstream. NULL (default), samples treated independent, e.g. cell culture experiments. replicate_col Optional: name column sample_ann identifying replicate IDs. provided, column renamed 'Replicate'. NULL (default), function looks column named 'Replicate'; absent, replicate IDs auto-generated within Group Time (Subject, provided). batch_col Optional: name column sample_ann identifying batch information. provided, column renamed 'Batch'. NULL (default), function looks column named 'Batch'; absent, samples assigned batch 1. feature_threshold Threshold calc_feature_property(). Feature values > feature_threshold considered expressed (default: 0). filter_ratio Minimum ratio time points feature must expressed , considered expressed group (default: 0.5, meaning feature must > feature_threshold >=50% time points group considered expressed). Passed group_specific_features(). min_groups Minimum number groups feature must expressed , filter_ratio, pass cross group filter (default: 2). Passed group_specific_features(). keep select features variance decomposition: "below_quantile" (default): keep features residual variance residual_threshold quantile (0-1 scale). "top_n": keep top n_keep lowest-residual features. "threshold": keep features residual percentage residual_threshold (0-100 scale; use 100 skip filtering). residual_threshold Numeric: keep = "below_quantile", quantile residual variance use cutoff (0-1 scale). keep = "threshold", percentage cutoff (0-100 scale, 100 = keep features). (default: NULL, auto-assigned 0.75 "below_quantile", 100 "threshold") n_keep Number features keep keep = "top_n" (default: 5000). interaction Passed decomp_variance(): TRUE, adds (1|Group:Time) ((1|Subject:Time) Subject present) interaction term (default: FALSE). n_cores Number cores variance decomposition (default: 1).

title: TiDEomics 0.99.0
text: NEW FEATURES Added NEWS.md file track changes package. SIGNIFICANT USER-VISIBLE CHANGES New package. Initial submission Bioconductor. BUG FIXES bug fixes. See details http://bioconductor.org/developers/package-guidelines/#news.

title: TiDEomics 0.99.1
text: Added input validation user-facing function arguments descriptive errors. Added match.arg() fixed-set arguments (theme_custom$legend_position, prepare_WGCNA$networkType). Added assay parameter + .match_assay() plot_cor_matrix(). Replaced WGCNA::unsignedKME() (unexported) abs(WGCNA::signedKME()). Removed S4Vectors:: calls; added S4Vectors, SingleCellExperiment Suggests. Fixed roxygen inconsistencies (defaults, return types). Added test coverage uncovered branches across multiple functions. Reordered vignette; fixed prepare_tide mapping table assay naming notes.

title: TiDEomics 0.99.2
text: NEW FEATURES plot_modules_h() now supports multi-category enrichment annotation via enrich_category parameter, accepts vector category names (e.g. c("BP", "CC", "Hub features")). Multiple enrichment columns displayed side--side single annotation block using new internal .anno_multicol_textbox system. new enrich_p_threshold parameter controls per-category p-value colour-coding enrichment terms. plot_modules_h() can now display hub features dedicated column enrichment textbox via enrich_category = "Hub features", using mark_features colours anno_mark. hub features shown textbox, left-side anno_mark automatically suppressed. New internal function .module_labels() normalises orders module labels: numeric labels ordered value, WGCNA colour names preserve original order. prefix parameter controls "M" prefixing. extract_hubs() extracts top N hub features per WGCNA module using intra-modular connectivity (kME). Returns character vector suitable mark_features plot_modules_h(). enrich_rank_by enrich_top_n plot_modules_h() now accept per-category vectors matching length enrich_category, enabling different ranking columns top-N cutoffs enrichment column. as_DeeDeeExperiment() converts prepare_tide() output DeeDeeExperiment object. DE results flattened nested contrast--time format columns renamed DeeDeeExperiment convention (logFC → log2FoldChange, etc.). Enrichment results enrichGO_list() automatically unwrapped. New .check_numeric() validator numeric arguments; .check_* validation added across remaining exported functions previously unchecked arguments (extract_hubs, WGCNA_module, decomp_variance, create_input, calc_feature_property, split_groups, plot_trend, plot_volcano, plot_breakpoints, plot_DE_between_group, prepare_WGCNA, impute_groups, enrichGO_rank, enrichR_list, prepare_tide, plot_pca_3D). prepare_tide() provides end--end data preparation: creates SummarizedExperiment, normalises starting time point, filters features detection completeness (via group_specific_features()) residual variance, returns unmerged (replicate-level) merged (mean per Group-Time) outputs ready downstream analysis. enrich_msigdb(): hypergeometric enrichment MSigDB via msigdbr, species/db_species support plot_modules_h()-compatible output. summarise_module_metrics(): per-module kME statistics (MeanKME, MeanKME2, MedianKME, SDKME, MinKME, MaxKME). Auto-detects signed/unsigned networks; preserves kME sign. SIGNIFICANT USER-VISIBLE CHANGES WGCNA_module() now returns modules ordered decreasing module size instead alphabetically, matching WGCNA convention. Module column retains bare numeric labels (e.g. "0", "1", "2") backwards compatibility. plot_modules_h() now normalises module labels internally .module_labels() automatically excludes grey module ("M0"). multi-category enrichment system supersedes previous single-category path. New internal annotation infrastructure anno_multicol_textbox.R provides local .textbox_grob (avoids ComplexHeatmap::: internals), .reformat_cat_terms, .anno_multicol_textbox building multi-column enrichment annotations. .module_labels() gained prefix parameter control "M"-prefixing; WGCNA colour names now preserve first-appearance order instead silently alphabetised factor(). DE_between_group() now returns ref_groups all_groups elements cleaner downstream use plot_DE_between_group(). plot_pca() plot_umap() longer plot parameter; always return list p_list (named list ggplot objects) pca / umap_layout (underlying data). Use $pca $umap_layout access data previously returned plot = FALSE. BUG FIXES plot_modules_h(): mark_features plain character vector enrich_category includes "Hub features", features now correctly appear textbox column (previously silently dropped). extract_hubs(): fixed bug missing kME column cause error instead skipping module message. DE_between_group(): fixed tb_name → t typo causing “object found” error; return element renamed ref_groups (plural) consistency. WGCNA_module(): fixed loss feature names (row.names) using .module_labels(), caused empty downstream data. summarise_module_pattern(): fixed apply/table/data.frame edge-case bug (error single-column input) replacing tidyr::unite() + dplyr::count(). Removed print_top_n/top_n arguments. plot_volcano(): group/time arguments now conditionally validated missing(), .check_character applied active parameter set. plot_modules_h(): enrichment annotation blocks now filtered exclude modules terms across categories (previously showed empty textboxes). .check_positive() now accepts vectors (previously required scalar length 1), fixing prepare_WGCNA(powers = seq(1, 20)). .match_assay() fixed: numeric assay indices unnamed assays now kept -instead resolving NA empty string. example_obj.rda regenerated properly named assays (c("orig", "norm")) matching current create_input() output. Data generation script (inst/script/tutorial_input.R) updated GEOquery v2 (returns SummarizedExperiment; uses colData() instead pData()). plot_modules_h(): known issue — blank plot may appear heatmap RStudio enrich_list provided. upstream ComplexHeatmap behaviour (physical-device measurement anno_link RStudio, introduced v2.5.x). Saving directly file using knitr/R Markdown avoids . prepare_tide() uses group_specific_features() ID filtering step min_groups parameter (default 2), replacing inline dplyr logic. min_groups validated exceed number groups. Non-ASCII characters removed R source files: right arrow (-> replaces U+2192), multiplication sign (x replaces U+00D7), approximately-equal (~ replaces U+2248). Em dashes already removed previous update. Tutorial data (tutorial_data) now normalised log2(CPM + 1) (counts-per-million pseudocount, log2-transformed) instead raw counts, providing realistic starting point demonstration. Assays now named "orig" (original data) "norm" (normalised--start data). DE_between_time(), DE_between_group(), decomp_variance() longer default assay. names numeric indices accepted across functions. Computation separated visualization: DE_between_group() longer produces inline plot; use new plot_DE_between_group() function instead. plot fontsize arguments removed. create_input() now replicate_col batch_col arguments, allowing custom column names replicate batch information (matching existing subject_col pattern). match.arg() now used fixed-choice arguments: method plot_cor_matrix(), facet_by plot_distribution(), confidence decouple_score(), category enrichGO_list() enrichGO_rank(). Input validation added across exported functions: SummarizedExperiment type checks, p-value range checks (0–1), positive-integer checks, logical-flag checks, descriptive errors incorrect argument types, provenance checks (e.g., calc_feature_property() validates input produced merge_replicates(), run_Trendy() validates imputed data). DE_between_time() DE_between_group() now warn selected assay appears contain un-logged raw counts (limma requires log-transformed, normalised input). magrittr dependency fully removed. %>% replaced native |> pipe throughout package vignettes. Magrittr helper functions replaced base R equivalents (set_names/set_colnames -> stats::setNames, set_rownames -> base, extract2 -> nrow). Single-plot functions now return() plot objects instead print() side effects (plot_trend, plot_cor_matrix, plot_cv, plot_distribution, plot_variance, plot_volcano, plot_breakpoints). enables programmatic composition testing returned plots. Documentation Bioconductor installation instructions added README vignette. Data generation scripts moved data-raw/ inst/script/, new scripts generating example_net example_res_list used @examples. @examples longer include downstream function calls. Removed sessioninfo Suggests. Vignette restructured two paths: one-step prepare_tide() wrapper manual step--step, cross-references . @returns formatting standardised plain prose across functions (replacing \describe{\item{...}} blocks). Assays now stored matrices instead data.frames throughout pipeline, fixing iSEE compatibility. enrichGO_list() now returns unmerged_all unmerged_simplified (lists enrichResult objects) DeeDeeExperiment compatibility. .prepare_gene_list() drops empty factor levels filtering, eliminating spurious “Gene list 0 empty” messages. enrich_msigdb() removed redundant qvalue column; qvalue dropped Suggests. BUG FIXES as_DeeDeeExperiment(): fixed reducedDims() found (DDE 1.3.0 NAMESPACE bug), (se, "SCE") coercion failure, empty de_results rejection, enrichR column mapping DDE compatibility. plot_distribution(), plot_missing(), plot_ID(), plot_cv(): added .data.frame() matrix assay → dplyr compatibility. plot_cv(): fixed . pronoun native pipe (replaced rownames_to_column()). plot_umap(): fixed p1 variable reference circle=TRUE path. plot_breakpoints(): empty-list input now errors meaningfully. plot_modules_h(): Hub features Legend lacked labels argument. Documentation Vignette: added enrich_msigdb() section.
